cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to God's church in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's just said that he and the Corinthians alike should cleanse themselves from everything that defiles body and spirit (2 Corinthians 7:1). Now he gets personal: "Make room for us in your hearts."

cards.question: Paul asks the Corinthians to make room for his team in their hearts. True or false: he says his team has wronged no one.

cards.text: Then Paul makes sure they know he's not saying this to condemn them. It's like texting somebody "We need to talk" and then racing to send "NOTHING BAD! Nothing bad! I promise!"

cards.question: Paul doesn't want the Corinthians to feel accused. How does he describe the place they hold in his team's hearts?

answers.text: So close they live and die together
Like trusted partners in the work
Like guests who are always welcome

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians his confidence in them is great and his pride in them is great. True or false: he says that in all his troubles his joy runs dry.

cards.text: Paul looks back: when his team arrived in Macedonia, their bodies had no rest, and they were pressed. Friend, I'm a cookie STAMPER, pressing is my whole JOB, and even I'm saying that's too much pressing.

cards.question: In Macedonia, Paul's team had no rest. What does Paul say they faced?

cards.text: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted Paul's team. Two little words, BUT GOD, and the whole mood changes.

cards.question: God comforted Paul's team in Macedonia when someone arrived. Who was it?

cards.text: Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23), didn't show up empty-handed: the Corinthians had comforted him, and he brought their news with him. That's the friend who shows up AND brings the good cookies.

cards.question: Titus tells Paul about the Corinthians. What does he report?

answers.text: Their longing and zeal for Paul
Their plans to stop writing Paul

cards.question: Hearing Titus's news about the Corinthians, Paul ___ all the more.

cards.text: Now Paul brings up a letter he sent the Corinthians before this one. And that letter caused them sorrow.

cards.question: Paul's letter caused the Corinthians sorrow. How does Paul say he feels about it?

answers.text: He wants them to forget it
He plans to take it back

cards.text: But Paul admits he did regret it: he sees his letter caused them sorrow, but only for a short time. That's ALL of us after hitting send, staring at the screen going oh no, oh no, what did I DO.

cards.question: Paul says that now he rejoices, but not because the Corinthians were made sorrowful. So what is he rejoicing about?

answers.text: Their sorrow led them to repentance
His letter proved that he was right

cards.text: Paul says the Corinthians felt the sorrow that God had intended. Not just ANY sorrow, friend, the very sorrow GOD had in mind.

cards.question: The Corinthians felt the sorrow God had intended. True or false: Paul says they were harmed by his letter.

cards.text: Then Paul lays out two kinds of sorrow. And friend, they do NOT end up at the same address.

cards.question: Paul says godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to ___ without regret.
Godly sorrow leads to salvation. What does Paul say worldly sorrow brings?

cards.text: Paul says look at what this godly sorrow has produced in them: earnestness, eagerness to clear themselves, indignation, alarm, longing, zeal, vindication! He's running down that list like a HYPE MAN, and the Corinthians are the main event!

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that in every way they have proved themselves to be ___ in this matter.
Paul says he didn't write his letter on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed. So why did he write it?

answers.text: So they'd see how devoted they were to him
So they'd stop doubting that he was an apostle
So other churches would hear what happened

cards.text: So Paul's encouraged. And Titus came back with his spirit refreshed by every one of the Corinthians, and I bet he walked in looking like a fresh batch straight out of the oven.

cards.question: The Corinthians refreshed Titus's spirit. True or false: Paul says the joy of Titus left him even more delighted.

cards.text: Turns out Paul had boasted to Titus about the Corinthians. Friend, you know how SCARY it is to talk somebody up and then just stand there hoping they don't make you look silly?

cards.question: Paul had boasted to Titus about the Corinthians. True or false: Paul says he ended up embarrassed by what he had said.

cards.text: Just as everything Paul said to the Corinthians was true, his boasting to Titus proved true as well. That's the DREAM, friend: you brag on somebody, and they show up and make you look like a GENIUS.
And Titus's affection for the Corinthians is even greater when he remembers how they welcomed him.

cards.question: Titus remembers how the Corinthians welcomed him. How does Paul describe that welcome?

answers.text: All obedient with fear and trembling
All hesitant with doubts and questions
All proud with boasting and praise

cards.question: Paul wraps up by rejoicing that he can have ___ confidence in the Corinthians.
